title: Static Generation and Rendering Strategies
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of Static Generation and Rendering Strategies in a Vue 3 application.
Apply at least one of the syllabus subtopics in a small, inspectable example.
Verify one expected behavior and identify a relevant edge case.

content.intro: This lesson studies Static Generation and Rendering Strategies within Server-Side Rendering, Nuxt, and Deployment. The source PDF subtopics are preserved below and connected to an original working-style example.
content.why_it_matters: Rendering choices affect initial content, hydration, deployment complexity, caching, security, and the availability of browser-only APIs.

content_blocks.title: Static Generation and Rendering Strategies: Server rendering and hydration
content_blocks.alt_text: Server rendering and hydration diagram for lesson 141: Static Generation and Rendering Strategies. Render deterministic HTML for this request → Send markup without shared mutable user state → Attach events to matching initial output
content_blocks.caption: Rendering flow: server output and client hydration must agree, and per-request state must remain isolated.

content_blocks.title: The idea in context
content_blocks.text: Vue rendering may be client-side, server-rendered, or pre-rendered; Nuxt provides an opinionated application framework for SSR/SSG use cases. This lesson focuses on Static Generation and Rendering Strategies. Start by naming the state, component, browser behavior, or deployment boundary involved; then predict what should change and test the smallest example.

items.title: Pre-rendered pages
items.text: For Pre-rendered pages, connect the term to a visible behavior in a small Vue 3 example. State what input or reactive dependency changes, predict the UI result, and verify the prediction with a normal case plus a boundary case.

items.title: Hybrid rendering concepts
items.text: For Hybrid rendering concepts, express the intended DOM result through a Vue template binding instead of directly manipulating the DOM. Keep template expressions small, use stable keys for stateful list items, and choose directives based on whether content should be created, removed, or merely hidden.

items.title: Choosing rendering strategies by route
items.text: For Choosing rendering strategies by route, keep the URL as the addressable navigation state, use named route records when practical, and handle invalid parameters or failed navigation explicitly. A route guard improves navigation flow but does not replace backend access control.

content_blocks.expected_output: The viewport width is read only in the browser after mount, avoiding a server-side reference to window.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Use the snippet in a Vue SFC. Test server and browser behavior separately; if rendered state depends on time/randomness, ensure hydration output is deterministic.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the initial values or original code, reload the development app/test, and repeat once with a boundary or failure case. Remove temporary logs and test data before committing.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Work through Static Generation and Rendering Strategies with a predict–change–verify loop. First state the expected UI or console output. Change only the relevant input/state value, then observe the result. Compare it with the expected output in the code block; if it differs, check the exact file, runtime/version, browser Console, and network response before widening the investigation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Extend the example to include “Hybrid rendering concepts”. Keep the same behavior for the ordinary input, then try an empty, invalid, repeated, or failure condition that makes sense for the example. Record the expected result before testing.

items.title: Assuming behavior instead of checking it
items.text: Write down the expected result and reproduce the issue in the smallest possible example; inspect the browser Console and the exact reactive value or request.

items.title: Ignoring an edge case
items.text: Try empty input, a missing item, repeated interaction, a failed request, or unmounting while work is pending; handle the case explicitly.

items.title: Putting every responsibility in one component
items.text: Separate display, reusable logic, API service, and shared state when that boundary makes the behavior easier to test and explain.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember: Vue rendering may be client-side, server-rendered, or pre-rendered; Nuxt provides an opinionated application framework for SSR/SSG use cases. For Static Generation and Rendering Strategies, keep the example small, verify the rendered or logged result, and consult the official references when behavior depends on a specific Vue or ecosystem version.

content_blocks.title: Accessibility, version, and runtime notes
content_blocks.text: Use semantic HTML, readable labels, keyboard-operable controls, and visible errors where the example interacts with users. Vue examples are intended for Vue 3.x with create-vue/Vite unless a legacy or specialist lesson explicitly says otherwise. This CodeLeaf playground does not execute arbitrary Vue code; the snippets are labeled for static validation and should be run in a separate local project.

content.task: Create a small example for “Static Generation and Rendering Strategies” that applies “Pre-rendered pages”, predicts the expected result, and verifies a relevant boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the named Vue concept rather than only mentioning it.
The expected output or observable behavior is written down and can be checked locally.
At least one boundary, loading, invalid-input, or failure case is tested or explicitly reasoned about.
The example uses semantic/accessible interaction patterns and does not treat frontend state as authoritative security.
hints: Start with the smallest observable part of “Pre-rendered pages”.
Predict the output before changing one input at a time.
Use the browser Console, Vue DevTools, or the appropriate test runner to isolate a mismatch.

common_mistakes.problem: The example only covers the happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Real interfaces receive empty values, delayed responses, invalid input, and failed requests.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one realistic edge/failure case and state its expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: The code assumes an API or feature exists in every runtime.
common_mistakes.why: Tool and API support depends on Vue, the build tool, or the chosen SSR/test framework.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the linked official reference and record the runtime/version assumption.

summary: Static Generation and Rendering Strategies belongs to the broader area Server-Side Rendering, Nuxt, and Deployment.
The main concept to practice is Pre-rendered pages.
Verify a normal result and one meaningful boundary case before using the pattern in a production feature.
